reason: This passage (Exodus 2:1-10, the birth and rescue of Moses) portrays Pharaoh's daughter—the primary elite character—quite favorably. She is depicted as compassionate (וַתַּחְמֹל עָלָיו—'she had compassion on him'), merciful in rescuing the Hebrew child despite the apparent context of persecution, and ultimately maternal in adopting him. While the passage implicitly references Pharaoh's decree to kill Hebrew males, that backdrop does not extend to an unfavorable portrayal within the text itself. Rather, Pharaoh's daughter emerges as one of the story's heroes. The Levite family (the other significant characters) are also portrayed favorably—depicted as righteous and loving toward their child.
